description:
memory.rs:318-334 — find_uniqueness_conflict iterates every Metadata object in the account and computes UniquenessKey for each, returning the first match. O(N) per /set create, called once per create entry. For a /set call creating M new objects against an account holding N existing Metadata, that's O(M*N).

Reference-impl context: this is the in-memory backend used for tests and demos. Real backends will have a (relatedType, relatedId, type_name, isPrivate) → id index that makes this O(1). The MemoryBackend doesn't need to mirror that complexity.

Why this is P3 not P2: the documented purpose of MemoryBackend is integration tests and demos, not production. Tests run with N=5 to N=20. The O(M*N) bound is invisible at that scale.

Worth flagging because:
1. The function name and signature look like a candidate-copy target for a real backend's secondary-index lookup. A contributor copying find_uniqueness_conflict into a Postgres backend would inherit a 'iterate every row' pattern.
2. The cargo-cult-warning convention is already established for demo_next_id (memory.rs:253-258, the multi-line NOT A PRODUCTION PATTERN comment block). Apply the same convention here: a doc comment block explaining the demo-grade limitation and pointing at what a real backend should index.

Fix: add a rustdoc block on find_uniqueness_conflict matching the demo_next_id pattern: warn against copy-paste, sketch the production shape (HashMap<UniquenessKey, Id> maintained alongside ). No code change to the impl itself — the linear scan IS the demo pattern.

Severity: P3 because:
- Performance is not in scope for a demo-grade in-memory backend.
- The risk is contributor-template-copying, not user-facing performance regression.
- Single comment block fixes it.
title: MemoryBackend.find_uniqueness_conflict is O(N) linear scan; no secondary index
